segments.line: Two days later, Ellie doesn't come back from the market.
Felix runs every street around the Circus.
Tullia asks every shopkeeper. Nobody saw anything.
Then a boy you've never seen walks up to the counter and puts down
a little coral hair tie. Ellie's.
Next to it, a wax tablet. The contract. Unsigned.
You know what it means.
Sign, and Ellie comes home tonight. Don't sign, and you might never see her again.
But if you sign, Tullia loses the shop her husband built.
Every cook on this street loses everything.
And the most powerful men in Rome get a machine that turns hungry crowds into loyal ones.
Maybe you just taught an empire a new way to control people.
You think about every time travel movie you've ever seen. Don't change history. Don't help the bad guys.
Easy to say, when it isn't your sister.
Tullia puts a hand on your shoulder. 'Family first, ' she says. 'Shops can be rebuilt. '
So you sign.
That evening, Ellie walks back through the door with another honey cake, completely fine. She thinks she was at a party.
You hug her so hard she complains.
Then a messenger arrives from the palace. The emperor is throwing a feast tonight, and he wants two hundred burgers.
Cooked fresh, here, on your grill. All night.
Outside, a hot, dry wind is blowing. You ask Felix what day it is. He thinks for a moment.
'The eighteenth of July. '
